 --> Motilal Oswal, CAMS, other capital market stocks rise up to 5% as benchmarks sustain at 8-month high
 The robust FII inflows have pushed the Nifty 50 and Sensex indexes up 9.6% and 10%, respectively, so far in November 
 J Jagannath 
 November 12, 2026 / 10:17 IST Share --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 Motilal Oswal, CAMS, other capital market stocks rise up to 5% as benchmarks sustain at 8-month high Capital market stocks rose up to 4% on November 12.
 Sensex and Nifty sustained at an eight-month high.
 FIIs net bought $6.43 billion of shares in November.

 Capital market stocks like Motilal Oswal , Nuvama, CAMS rose up to 4% on November 12 as benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty were sustaining at eight-month high.
 At 10 am on November 12, the Nifty Capital Markets index was trading 1.1% higher at 5,899.1 with Nuvama, CAMS, Motilal Oswal Financial Services leading the gains by climbing 4%, 3.9% and 3.8%, respectively.
 At 10:04 am, the Sensex was up 403.23 points or 0.49% at 82,282.63, and the Nifty was up 111.40 points or 0.44% at 25,366.45, their highest level since February 27, 2026. About 2,389 shares advanced, 1,063 shares declined, and 180 shares were unchanged.
 Foreign portfolio investors bought Rs 12,563 crore worth of Indian shares on Wednesday, provisional data showed. They have net bought $6.43 billion of shares in November, already their biggest monthly purchase since September 2024.
 The robust inflows have pushed the Nifty 50 and Sensex indexes up 9.6% and 10%, respectively, so far in November.

 Other gainers on the sectoral index were CDSL, Kfin Tech, Nippon Life India Asset Management, which climbed 3.4%, 2.8% and 2.5%, respectively.
 "The Nifty rally of 9.55% in seven trading sessions so far in November is being led primarily by the aggressive buying by the FIIs. The tug of war between the FIIs and DIIs till November saw the FIIs on the sell side and DIIs on the buy side. Now, the positions have been completely reversed with FIIs turning aggressive buyers and DIIs turning consistent sellers. This FIIs vs DIIs position will set the market trend in the near-term. FIIs have already invested Rs 65,735 crore in Indian equities so far in November. This trend is likely to continue and has the potential to reach an all-time high number. Impressive earnings growth as evidenced by the good Q2 results and the macro relief from lower crude prices (Brent around $92) will support the rally. DIIs may continue profit booking putting brakes on the rally," said V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments Limited.
